Squirtle Is an Offspring of One the Most Beautiful Campers out There – Born of French Camping Design
14 photos
Photo: Carapate Aventure
Over the years, there have been hundreds if not thousands of camper models that I've written about, and very few have stood out quite like the Carapate. Well, I recently encountered some of their “newer” models, and one of which is the Squirtle or Squirt, for short.
Folks, Carapate is the name of a camper but also a brand and ever since they hit the scene years ago, they stood apart from all others with a travel trailer design that took us back to a time when camping was all about stripping away everything that cities have impregnated onto our soul and invited us to take in the very essence of the natural world.
Photo: Carapate Aventure The way the body is completed was and is one of the strongpoints for the style, with a pod-like structure that includes an oversized hatch along one side in order to open up the interior to the world around and allow us to take in all the beauty right from bed. It’s a clear reason why countless readers tune in every time we shed light on the Carapate.
While the Carapate is the flagship of the brand and has stood as the one and only unit from the brand, I recently checked back in with the French brand and come to find out, there are some “new” units available, and if I may, they still tap into the spirit of Carapate and all that this brand is about. Sources mention these models as having been around since 2024; I'm not so sure how we missed them until now.
I will shed light on the other two models that accompany the Squirt (Carapuce) over the next few days, but for now, we’ll focus primarily on this camping option as it's the most affordable in the lineup, the smallest, but also, is the only one that breaks away from the Carapate design , the one that landed them on the map. Will the Squirt take them off the radar? Let’s find out.
Photo: Carapate Aventure Right from the start, we can see that for the Squirt, the whole utility trailer style has been called upon, granting us access to a large box where we find all the systems the manufacturer offers, along with storing personal belongings, and any extras you ask for, while the upper level, or the sleeping area, is granted by the presence of a roof-top tent mounted onto a rack system.
Now, that box is still crafted from the choice material of this brand: wood. While most potential camper owners would freak out about hearing that their unit is built from wood, Carapate clearly treats this material to stand up to the elements, and if anything does need replacing, it’s easy to do.
The slide-out drawers are also crafted from this timeless building block, and it’s also here that we find access to some of the features we’ll be using while living off the land. This includes our cooking and dining gear only, and if you do ask for a fridge or cooler, it’ll be mounted outside and on the trailer’s drawbar or wherever you manage to mount it.
Photo: Carapate Aventure More wood is also found in shape of five tables or “shelves,” as Carapate calls them. These shelves are to line the lower edge of the Squirt and, if I may, are a pretty neat addition to the unit, especially for hanging around and putting a beer or book down. Dishware also falls into this category.
All this wood, chassis, and running gear make up for a camper that can weigh as little as 340 kg (750 lbs), and since it peaks at 800 kg (1,764 lbs) – it's a braked-axle trailer – it leaves us with ample cargo space more than the camper weighs on its own. Speaking of cargo, most of which will be stuffed into the box via a hatch found at the rear.
What I found rather interesting and wild about this little trailer is the fact that Carapate showcases it with features like solar panels, leading me to believe that batteries are in place and unlocking off-grid use. You’ll need to bring along plenty of water.
Photo: Carapate Aventure This leaves us with just a couple more important aspects of the Squirtle, one of which is the fact that, due to the use of the rooftop tent, this camper is limited to use in the warmer months of the year. The second is the price. According to Carapate’s website, the Squirtle is starts off at no more than €10,600, or roughly $11,900.
I’m curious to find out how you feel about that price so drop your thoughts in the comment section below.
Actually, there is one other aspect we can add to the list of traits of the Squirt, and it’s that Americans should have a very difficult time making one their own. Then again, there are several brands in the US that craft similar campers, although aluminum and steel are called upon to complete them.
Luckily, if you do want to build your own wooden Squirtle-like camper, it's clearly possible; show a couple of images to a craftsman in your area and see if you folks can make it a reality.
